_note: Drizzle vs Kysely evaluation for TECHNOLOGY-DECISIONS section 3, run against PostgreSQL 17.11 + pgvector 0.8.6 after TypeScript/Node was selected. Probe source: spikes/.state/dataaccess/probe.mjs (transient working directory; the findings are recorded here).

drizzle-kit.scope: devDependency only - not shipped at runtime

required_postgres_behaviour._note: Every capability Ferret's knowledge engine depends on. Both candidates passed all six.

drizzle.detail: drizzle-kit generate produced correct DDL for a schema containing tsvector and vector(3) columns plus a GIN index, once both non-builtin types were declared via customType. Generated: CREATE TABLE doc (id integer PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, body text, tsv "tsvector", embedding vector(3)); CREATE INDEX doc_tsv_idx ON doc USING gin (tsv).
drizzle.significance: This was the decisive test. Ferret's schema is not ordinary relational - it needs tsvector, pgvector and GIN. Drizzle's schema diffing handles them rather than forcing an escape hatch for the core model.

kysely.detail: Kysely ships a Migrator that runs migration files but performs no schema diffing; every migration is hand-written SQL/TypeScript.
kysely.significance: No risk of the generator mis-modelling an exotic type, but every schema change across the canonical-model Epics is manual.

assessment.reason: TECHNOLOGY-DECISIONS section 3 lists migration quality first among the selection criteria. Ferret's canonical model spans EPIC-006 through EPIC-010 and will change repeatedly under EPIC-010 schema versioning; generated, diffed, versioned migrations materially reduce that burden, and drizzle-kit was verified to handle Ferret's non-standard column types. Both candidates cover 100% of the required PostgreSQL behaviour, so coverage did not separate them.
known_tradeoffs: Drizzle's runtime is 6x larger than Kysely (9.9 MB vs 1.6 MB), though drizzle-kit's 9.8 MB stays out of the shipped package.
Apache-2.0 rather than MIT - permissive, but a second licence family in the tree.
tsvector and pgvector are not Drizzle builtins and must be declared via customType; that declaration is now proven but is a maintenance point if Drizzle changes the customType API.

Schema-first diffing can hide PostgreSQL behaviour, which TECHNOLOGY-DECISIONS section 3 explicitly warns against. Mitigation: FTS and vector queries are written as raw `sql` templates (verified working), keeping the query path explicit even where the schema path is generated.
assessment.reversal_condition: If drizzle-kit diffing proves unreliable for partial indexes, temporal tables or the provenance schema during EPIC-002 or EPIC-010, fall back to Kysely with hand-written migrations. Both were verified against identical requirements, so the fallback is a known-good path rather than a fresh evaluation.
